title: End-of-Budget speeches after Supply and Supplementary Bills pass
what_it_is: Speeches at the end of the formal Budget 2026 process, after the Supply Bill and Supplementary Bill were passed, with the Leader of the House acknowledging the Speaker and the Speaker reflecting on the debate.
stage: End of the formal Budget process for Budget 2026
why_it_matters: The record says Budget 2026 is intended to help Singaporeans navigate a changed world, with measures on AI adoption, economic strategy, workers, families, social compact, security and sustainability. It also says the projected $15.1 billion surplus for FY2025 provides ballast and buffer against potential turbulence, and that global developments may affect energy prices, business costs and daily costs of living.

key_points.point: The passing of the Supply Bill and Supplementary Bill marks the end of the formal Budget process for Budget 2026.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: the passing of the Supply Bill and the Supplementary Bill a few moments ago marks the end of the formal Budget process for Budget 2026.

key_points.point: The Budget passed included more than $200 billion in Estimates, with specified Main and Development Estimates amounts.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: we have passed a Budget with more than $200 billion worth of Estimates – $158,962,520,000 for the Main Estimates and $49,014,559,600 for the Development Estimates.

key_points.point: The Leader described it as the largest annual Budget to date, passed amid a changed and uncertain world.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: This is our largest annual Budget to date, passed against the backdrop of a profoundly changed and uncertain world.

key_points.point: Budget 2026 aims to harness AI as a strategic advantage and drive national adoption.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: Budget 2026 aims to harness AI as a strategic advantage and drive national adoption so that Singaporeans can take full advantage of the opportunities afforded by technology.

key_points.point: Budget 2026 allows implementation of a refreshed economic strategy, continued investment in workers, job creation, family support, social compact, security and sustainability.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: Budget 2026 also allows us to implement our refreshed economic strategy, continue investing in our workers and drive growth to create jobs, strengthen support for families and advance our social compact, and enhance our security and sustainability.

key_points.point: Budget 2026 spotlighted the total fertility rate at a historic low of 0.87 and signals the start of the marriage and parenthood reset as a whole-of-nation effort.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: Budget 2026 also put a spotlight on our total fertility rate (TFR), which has dropped to a historic low of 0.87 and signals the start of the marriage and parenthood reset as a whole-of-nation effort.

key_points.point: A projected surplus of $15.1 billion for FY2025 was reported.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: We have projected a healthy surplus of $15.1 billion for financial year (FY) 2025.

key_points.point: The Leader cited the US Supreme Court striking down President Trump's Liberation Day tariffs on 20 February.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: On 20 February, eight days after the Budget Statement, the US Supreme Court struck down President Trump's Liberation Day tariffs.

key_points.point: The Leader cited US and Israel strikes against Iran on 28 February.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: On 28 February, the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran.

key_points.point: The Leader said these developments added to the overall climate of uncertainty.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: These developments have added to the overall climate of uncertainty.

key_points.point: The Leader said if energy prices are affected, there will be implications for business costs and daily costs of living.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: If so, there will be implications for business costs and daily costs of living.

key_points.point: The Leader said Singapore will feel the knock-on impacts keenly as a small and open economy.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: As a small and open economy, Singapore will feel the knock-on impacts keenly.

key_points.point: The Leader said the approach of fiscal prudence has been validated repeatedly.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: Our approach of fiscal prudence has been validated time and time again.

key_points.point: The Leader reported that 425 cuts were covered over six days of Committee of Supply, with almost 55 hours of debate.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: 425 cuts were covered over six days of Committee of Supply, with almost 55 hours of debate.

key_points.point: The Leader said there was no formal break in the Budget process for the first time in her recollection.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: And for the first time in my recollection, there was no formal break in the Budget process.

key_points.point: The Speaker said there was unanimous support from both sides of the House for Budget 2026.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: there was unanimous support from both sides of the House for Budget 2026.

key_points.point: The Speaker said this year's entire Budget and Committee of Supply debate took place within Ramadan for the first time.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: for the first time, this year’s entire Budget and Committee of Supply debate took place within the period of Ramadan.

key_points.point: The Speaker said total time needed for this year's Budget and Committee of Supply debate was 12% more than last year, though cuts were fewer by about a third.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: With more Members in this 15th Parliament, the total time that we needed for this year’s Budget and Committee of Supply debate was 12% more than last year, even though the number of cuts were fewer, by about a third.

key_points.point: The Speaker said there will be more debates, more Bills to pass and more challenges ahead.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: There will be more debates, more Bills to pass and more challenges ahead.

key_points.point: The Speaker said Members must leave the world in no doubt of their commitment to do what is best for Singapore.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: We must leave the world in no doubt of our commitment to do what is best for Singapore.

what_happens_next: The Leader of the House said the passing of the Supply Bill and the Supplementary Bill marks the end of the formal Budget process for Budget 2026; the Speaker said there will be more debates, more Bills to pass and more challenges ahead.
not_said: How will the projected $15.1 billion surplus for FY2025 be used?
What specific measures will implement the AI, economic strategy, worker, family, social compact, security and sustainability elements of Budget 2026?
How will the marriage and parenthood reset be delivered as a whole-of-nation effort?
What effects will the cited global developments have on energy prices, business costs and daily costs of living in Singapore?
What further debates and Bills are planned for the 15th Parliament?
